item.title: Fiji’s first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist Dr Nanise Sikiti to share her story on fijivillage Her-Story
item.description: From studying under a kerosene lamp in Levuka to becoming Fiji’s first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist, Dr Nanise Sikiti’s journey is one of sacrifice, resilience and determination. Dr Sikiti will share her inspiring story on fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono tonight at 7pm.
item.content:encoded:
From studying under a kerosene lamp in Levuka to becoming Fiji’s first in-country trained gynaecological oncologist, Dr Nanise Sikiti’s journey is one of sacrifice, resilience and determination.

Dr Sikiti will share her inspiring story on fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono tonight at 7pm.

Dr Sikiti will share the beginning of her journey in humble surroundings in Levuka.

She will also speak about the sacrifices she has made throughout her career, the challenges of balancing family and professional responsibilities, and the people and experiences that have shaped the woman and doctor she is today.

You can watch fijivillage Her-Story on our facebook page, YouTube channel, and TikTok and X account, fijivillage at 7pm tonight.

You can also catch the podcast, fijivillage Her-Story on Spotify and Apple Podcasts.

item.title: 6 children receive gift of life after free heart surgery
item.description: It was a joyous moment for six children after they received a new gift of life following free heart surgery at the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Heart Hospital. 12-year-old Raina Ram, 8-year-old Lepani Veiseyaki and 5-year-old Latileta Mausio of Fiji, 4-year-old Maria De Monfort Christopher, 2-month-old Takabo Mikaere of Kiribati, and 1-year-old Serah Duri of the Solomon Islands underwent surgeries pe
item.content:encoded:
It was a joyous moment for six children after they received a new gift of life following free heart surgery at the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Heart Hospital.

12-year-old Raina Ram, 8-year-old Lepani Veiseyaki and 5-year-old Latileta Mausio of Fiji, 4-year-old Maria De Monfort Christopher, 2-month-old Takabo Mikaere of Kiribati, and 1-year-old Serah Duri of the Solomon Islands underwent surgeries performed by medical teams from Australia and Singapore.

Ram’s mother, Ronita Chand, says her daughter was first diagnosed with Rheumatic Heart Disease after they took her to Labasa Hospital when she experienced difficulty breathing and sleeping.

She says Ram would get sick often, tire easily and was unable to play.

She is advising all parents to take their children for screening and early detection and to take any changes in their children’s health seriously.

Insert: her breathing is good now 9th sept

Meanwhile, Mausio’s mother, Laisa Yabakisiga, says her daughter was diagnosed with a heart condition after she was born.

She says Mausio underwent an echocardiogram at Lautoka Hospital and was then referred to the Heart Hospital, where she underwent surgery on Saturday.

She says her daughter is recovering well and her health has improved.

Insert: We are happy for her new life KK 9th Sept

Meanwhile, Kiribati medical carer Jennifer Kiata, who is in Fiji with Mikaere and her mother, Kaboiti, for Mikaere’s surgery, says the family is grateful that she has been given a new lease on life.

Kiata says the family back home is eagerly awaiting their return to celebrate Mikaere’s new life.

The Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Children’s Heart Hospital has so far performed 489 paediatric heart surgeries, 56,883 heart screenings and 85,715 medical consultations across Fiji.
